newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips lower, FOMC meeting brings jitters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips lower, FOMC meeting brings jitters.

text.p: U.S. blue chip shares edged down in nervous and quiet trading, taking their cues from a weaker bond market ahead of a key Federal Reserve policy-maker decision on short-term U.S. interest rates.

The Dow industrials were trading off around 56 points at 7170. Their early slide prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading at 0952 EDT/1352 GMT. But Nasdaq shares stood firmer, up nearly one point at 1342.
"Everyone is waiting for the Fed and there is a lot of volatility," Pierre Ellis, managing director and senior international economist at Primark Decision Economics, said.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the Fed policy arm which guides rates, convened at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT to discuss whether it needed to raise interest rates to combat inflation.
The results of the meeting were due around 1415 EDT/1815 GMT and analysts were divided over whether the FOMC would raise the federal funds rate 25 basis points or let it stand.
The long bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.95 percent in morning trade, depressing the stock market, traders said. But Nasdaq stayed positive, trading up 0.50 point to about 1342.
Ellis said markets were worried because the Fed could take a wide range of actions, and it was unclear what it would do.
